1→# Kain Architecture
2→
3→This file is the durable repo overview for `M:\Code\Kain`.
4→It is the fast way for future agents to understand what Kain is, where the important code lives, and which architectural rules matter enough to preserve.
5→
6→## What Kain Is
7→
8→Kain is a compiled multi-target language toolchain plus an embeddable runtime and host stack.
9→
10→The repo currently spans five connected layers:
11→
12→1. `crates/kain-core`
13→Language semantics, parsing, typing, effects, comptime, interpreter lanes, runtime-contract emission, shader metadata, and other compiler-owned truth.
14→
15→2. Importers and orchestration
16→`crates/kain-driver`, `crates/kain-omni`, `crates/kain-selfhost`, `crates/kain-build`, and importer crates turn source and manifests into emitted bundles, artifacts, and multi-runtime workflows.
17→
18→3. Runtime and host bridges
19→`runtime/native` is the canonical ABI floor and C runtime substrate. `crates/kain-host`, `crates/kain-sdk`, `crates/kain-reflect`, `crates/kain-c-ffi`, `crates/kain-crate-ffi`, `crates/kain-python`, `crates/kain-node`, and `crates/kain-interop` provide host/runtime integration.
20→
21→4. UI, native desktop, and 3D
22→`crates/kain-ui`, `crates/kain-ui-native`, and `crates/kain-3D` are the semantic UI and accelerated native presentation stack.
23→
24→5. Target adapters
25→`crates/web`, `crates/gpu`, `crates/kain-gpu-runtime`, and the `crates/ue5*` family consume compiler-owned contracts for specific runtime environments.
26→
27→## Non-Negotiable Ownership
28→
29→- `crates/kain-core` owns language meaning, typed metadata, capability requirements, and shader/compute-plan semantics.
30→- `crates/kain-driver` owns emitted bundle truth and app/runtime materialization.
31→- `runtime/native` owns the stable ABI floor, startup, service contracts, and low-level host/runtime substrate.
32→- Accelerated Rust lanes may optimize execution, but they must consume the same compiler-owned bundles rather than inventing a second semantic model.
33→- Web, UE5, selfhost, and future lanes are adapters, not alternate definitions of what Kain source means.
34→
35→## Main Folders
36→
37→- [README.md](/M:/Code/Kain/README.md): repo-level operating brief
38→- [repomap.md](/M:/Code/Kain/repomap.md): top-level folder map
39→- [MEMORY.md](/M:/Code/Kain/MEMORY.md): durable architectural task memory
40→- [docs/kainplan/ui_slate_x100](/M:/Code/Kain/docs/kainplan/ui_slate_x100): active UI overhaul docs, acceptance criteria, regression notes, and Gamma operator guidance
41→- [crates](/M:/Code/Kain/crates): workspace crates
42→- [runtime](/M:/Code/Kain/runtime): native runtime substrate, conformance, fixtures, and companion lanes
43→- [smoketest](/M:/Code/Kain/smoketest): capability proof matrix for bridges, UI, 3D, and mixed runtimes
44→- [smoketest/UI](/M:/Code/Kain/smoketest/UI): UI proof surface for authored shells, dense operator layouts, shader-canvas proofs, and packaged native launches
45→- [smoketest/allinone](/M:/Code/Kain/smoketest/allinone): broad regression harness that replays importers, standalone FFI bridges, GPU artifacts, Omni, Fabric, and UE5 codegen into per-lane output folders
46→- [docs](/M:/Code/Kain/docs): doctrine, plans, pipeline notes, validation notes, and research
47→- [apps](/M:/Code/Kain/apps): first-class applications and prototypes
48→- [apps/kain-fabric-modeler](/M:/Code/Kain/apps/kain-fabric-modeler): Fabric-first native 3D modeling app scaffold that converges Python, Kain, C ABI, Rust crate, GPU compute, Node, and native-ui packaging
49→- [apps/kain-fabric-dcc-suite](/M:/Code/Kain/apps/kain-fabric-dcc-suite): broader flagship Fabric-first DCC suite scaffold with scene, ingest, sculpt, material, rig, animation, sim, render, compositor, publish, automation, and tensor planning lanes
50→- [apps/kain-canvas-forge](/M:/Code/Kain/apps/kain-canvas-forge): Node-first desktop-ready painting and Three.js composition studio prototype that proves a browser and `.exe` app lane can live under `apps/`
51→- [stdlib](/M:/Code/Kain/stdlib): runtime support and standard library data
52→- [testing](/M:/Code/Kain/testing): test infrastructure and fixtures
53→
54→## Key Crates
55→
56→- [kain-core](/M:/Code/Kain/crates/kain-core): parser, AST, typechecker, comptime, runtime contract emission, realtime bundle metadata
57→- [kain-driver](/M:/Code/Kain/crates/kain-driver): target orchestration, shader bundles, native app materialization, packaged launcher snapshots, compute residency sidecars
58→- [cli](/M:/Code/Kain/crates/cli): `kain` command surface
59→- [kain-host](/M:/Code/Kain/crates/kain-host): Rust embedding and native function registration
60→- [kain-reflect](/M:/Code/Kain/crates/kain-reflect): reflection schemas and type identity
61→- [kain-sdk](/M:/Code/Kain/crates/kain-sdk): high-level embedding facade
62→- [kain-interop](/M:/Code/Kain/crates/kain-interop): shared buffer/image payload contracts
63→- [kain-gpu-runtime](/M:/Code/Kain/crates/kain-gpu-runtime): Vulkan compute executor consuming emitted shader bundles and residency metadata
64→- [kain-ui](/M:/Code/Kain/crates/kain-ui): semantic UI graph and patch-oriented UI meaning
65→- [kain-ui-native](/M:/Code/Kain/crates/kain-ui-native): native desktop host/runtime lane
66→- [kain-3D](/M:/Code/Kain/crates/kain-3D): native 3D renderer and viewport runtime
67→
68→## Primary Data Flows
69→
70→### Compile and runtime bundle flow
71→
72→`Kain source -> kain-core semantic analysis -> runtime contract / realtime app bundle / shader bundle metadata -> kain-driver materialization -> runtime/native and accelerated lanes consume the same bundle family`
73→
74→### Host bridge flow
75→
76→`.kn source -> compiler/runtime contracts -> host bridge crates (Python, Node, C ABI, Rust crate FFI) -> shared payload contracts via kain-interop`
77→
78→Current native-ui packaging rule for C ABI imports:
79→
80→- `kain-c-ffi` is no longer only an `Interpret`/`Test` lane concern. The Rust/native-ui packaging lane now emits packaged bridge manifests, copies bridge/shared-library sidecars into the app artifact set, and has the generated native app launcher load those packaged bridges before boot.
81→- This does not mean the current native UI host is a full general-purpose Kain interpreter. The lane is still bundle-driven; the packaging change makes foreign bridge dependencies explicit and shippable rather than hidden behind cache-local host-backed behavior.
82→
83→### Compute pipeline flow
84→
85→The current compute direction is:
86→
87→- authored compute truth starts in shader `comptime` metadata in `kain-core`
88→- `kain-core` emits workgroup, dispatch, tensor, stream, and neural metadata into realtime/shader-facing bundle structures
89→- `kain-driver` materializes compute residency sidecars and native app packaging data
90→- `runtime/native` validates and surfaces `primary_compute`
91→- `kain-gpu-runtime` is the real Vulkan dispatch bridge that consumes emitted shader/residency artifacts
92→
93→The architecture rule here is important: runtimes may execute the compute plan, but they must not become the source of truth for what that plan is.
94→
95→### Shader Canvas Lane
96→
97→The native shader-canvas UI lane now follows this contract:
98→
99→- `kain-ui` owns authored semantic surfaces and shader-canvas intent on canvas-like nodes
100→- `kain-core` emits explicit `shader_canvases` entries in `RealtimeAppBundle` so hosts do not have to rediscover shader-canvas bindings by guessing from local UI props
101→- `kain-core` also emits first-class shader-canvas text resources per surface: font atlas descriptors, text runs, declared runtime resource bindings, and optional asset-backed font references through the shared realtime asset catalog
102→- `kain-driver` materializes shader bundles and native app sidecars that keep shader-canvas metadata, shader refs, native UI bundles, and packaged realtime font assets aligned, resolving relative realtime asset sources against the authored source root instead of the materialization working directory
103→- `kain-ui-native` resolves shader canvases from realtime bundle metadata first and only falls back to surface-local shader refs when metadata is missing
104→- `kain-ui-native` now turns the shader-canvas text contract into real GPU inputs by serializing atlas/text metadata into the surface storage buffer and synthesizing a host-provisioned packed atlas texture, preferring packaged realtime font assets first, then `ab_glyph` rasterization from data-driven system-font aliases, with bitmap fallback and cache reuse across repeated surfaces that share atlas content
105→- `smoketest/UI/spv_ui_surface_probe` is the canonical native proof for this lane: it authors a real `<canvas>` node, packages a relative font asset, emits SPIR-V, and shows a fragment shader sampling the runtime-provided packed atlas texture
106→- canonical native shader payload remains SPIR-V, while the current WGPU native host may consume derived WGSL or runtime-transpiled WGSL from the same bundle family
107→
108→The architecture rule here is the same as the viewport and compute lanes: shader-canvas execution can optimize presentation, but it must stay subordinate to compiler-owned bundle truth rather than inventing a renderer-local UI shader dialect.
109→
110→### Semantic Tab Workspace Lane
111→
112→Semantic authored tabs now follow the same ownership rule:
113→
114→- `kain-ui` and `kain-core` own tab intent through authored node metadata such as `tab_group_id`, `tab_label`, `tab_order`, `tab_default_active`, and `persistent_layout_id`
115→- `kain-ui-native` may render that intent as native clickable tab chrome, but it should resolve and persist the active selection through `output.systems.workspace_layout.active_tabs`
116→- host-side tab rendering is allowed to optimize presentation, but it must not invent a second tab schema or bypass the emitted UI/runtime bundle truth
117→
118→`smoketest/UI/kinetic_ui_atlas` is now the durable repo-local proof for this lane: a fresh four-page native executable that uses semantic top tabs, docked shells, shader canvases, and a real viewport workspace without reusing the older smoketest compositions.
119→
120→### Reload-Safe UI Contract Lane
121→
122→UI reload and derived-value semantics now follow an explicit compiler-to-runtime contract:
123→
124→- `kain-core` emits stable signal ids, computed lowering (`writes_signal`, runtime `expr`, invalidation targets, scheduler phase), and event-route metadata including route ids, command routes, and transaction labels
125→- `kain-ui` owns runtime execution of those contracts, including derived recompute, exact invalidation, hot-reload state transfer, reload patch reporting, and bounded reconciliation
126→- `realtime_app_bundle.ui_contracts` now exposes computed, event-route, reload, focus, selection, overlay, motion, and workspace payloads so downstream native hosts can inspect semantic truth without rediscovering it from local widget state
127→
128→The architectural rule is the same as every other lane: reload behavior may be optimized by hosts, but the host must not become the source of truth for identity transfer, derived state, focus/selection state, or transaction semantics.
129→
130→`UiRuntimeBundle.native_projection` is now a compatibility-only sidecar rather than a normal bundle contract surface. Canonical serialization keeps `output.tree` and `output.systems` authoritative and omits the projection when it is empty; legacy raw-native consumers should opt into the explicit projection helper when they still need the flat view.
131→
132→### Native Packaging And Operator Loop
133→
134→The native packaging lane is the operator-facing loop for UI iteration:
135→
136→- `kain-driver` materializes native apps as a package set, writing the runtime bundle, runtime contract, realtime bundle, `app_manifest.json`, `runtime_snapshot.json`, and any required sidecars into the app artifact tree.
137→- Generated launchers resolve those packaged sidecars beside the executable so the app boots from authored bundle truth instead of a debug-host template.
138→- The runtime snapshot is the reload/control surface, not hidden launcher state. It carries explicit provider, session, workspace, command, and capability records, including the `runtime.reload` command already emitted by the packaging path.
139→- Devtools and inspectors must stay opt-in and remain represented in packaged truth, not injected as default product chrome.
140→- When a packaged launch stops reflecting a change, check the materialized manifest and snapshot sidecars first. That is the stable operator boundary before assuming the host itself is wrong.
141→
142→### Viewport Contract Lane
143→
144→Viewport startup intent now follows the same compiler-owned pattern:
145→
146→- `kain-core` emits `render.scenes` bindings with authored scene ids plus optional camera and presentation metadata
147→- `kain-ui-native` and `runtime/native` consume those bundle defaults first and only fall back to local scene/profile defaults when the bundle leaves a field unspecified
148→- scene ids, shader refs, camera presets, and presentation presets should travel together through the realtime bundle instead of being re-guessed independently by each host
149→
150→## Important Folders By Intent
151→
152→- [runtime/native](/M:/Code/Kain/runtime/native): canonical C runtime and ABI/service floor
153→- [runtime/conformance](/M:/Code/Kain/runtime/conformance): lane-level conformance harnesses
154→- [runtime/parallel](/M:/Code/Kain/runtime/parallel): Rust/Zig companion runtime work that must stay aligned with the native runtime doctrine
155→- [docs/kainplan](/M:/Code/Kain/docs/kainplan): active design and execution docs
156→- [docs/pipeline](/M:/Code/Kain/docs/pipeline): pipeline notes and operational docs
157→- [labs](/M:/Code/Kain/labs): focused validation labs
158→- [generated](/M:/Code/Kain/generated): disposable generated outputs
159→
160→## Common Commands
161→
162→Prefer the live CLI and source over stale docs when they disagree.
163→
164→Typical commands:
165→
166→- `kain doctor`
167→- `kain build`
168→- `kain build native-ui <file.kn>`
169→- `kain run <file.kn>`
170→- `kain gpu-artifacts <file.kn> --output <dir>`
171→- `kain selfhost phase1`
172→- `kain omni build`
173→- `kain fabric init --template polyglot`
174→- `kain fabric validate`
175→- `kain fabric run`
176→- `kain import-c`, `kain import-rust`, `kain import-ts`, `kain import-asm`, `kain import-crate`
177→- `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File smoketest/allinone/run_all.ps1`
178→
179→If the debug CLI is missing:
180→
181→- `cargo build -p cli`
182→- `target/debug/kain.exe --help`
183→
184→## Architectural Guardrails
185→
186→- Do not split semantic truth across runtime lanes.
187→- Do not let hosts re-parse source as the normal execution path.
188→- Do not invent lane-specific shader, UI, or compute metadata when compiler-owned bundles already exist.
189→- Prefer data-driven capabilities, manifests, registries, and bundle metadata over scattered string checks and host-local assumptions.
190→- Preserve the distinction between authored language semantics, importer behavior, and backend/runtime support.
191→- Platform- or console-specific render-command experiments should start as isolated adapter lanes under `smoketest/` or another dedicated adapter crate before any shared `kain-3D` contract is widened. The new `smoketest/3D/sm64_fast3d_smoke` is the pattern: it owns its own manifest, segment registry, display-list interpreter, and combiner logic instead of baking N64-specific assumptions into the common scene/material API too early.
192→- The SM64 import refresh workflow for that lane is now profile-driven and lives beside the smoke under `smoketest/3D/sm64_fast3d_smoke`. Use `refresh_sm64_import.bat` and `sm64_import_profile.render_us.json` instead of reconstructing long one-off `import-c` commands from memory.
193→- The same smoke now has a title-face extraction lane. `extract_sm64_title_face.bat`, `launch_title_face_visual_exe.bat`, and `capture_title_face_snapshot.bat` are the quickest path to a compiled proof that uses real extracted Mario face geometry while keeping N64-specific semantics inside the adapter.
194→- The adapter is no longer only a smoke-local runtime. The reusable host surface now lives in `crates/kain-fast3d-runtime`, while the smoke folder acts as a consumer that provides manifests, scripts, and validation assets.
195→- Keep the Fast3D lane data-driven. Its host startup now flows through crate-owned config files and env hooks (`KAIN_FAST3D_CONFIG`, `KAIN_FAST3D_MANIFEST`, `KAIN_FAST3D_SM64_ROOT`) rather than widening Kain language semantics or shared runtime contracts for one experimental console adapter.
196→- Native app launcher materialization now also supports generic host-sidecar packaging in `kain-driver`: generated launchers can copy arbitrary sidecars into the artifact/executable set, optionally export them as env vars, and switch between the default `run_bundled_app_json(...)` launcher path and a crate-owned no-arg entrypoint like `kain-fast3d-runtime::run_fast3d_cli()`. Preserve that mechanism as a generic host adapter capability, not a Fast3D-specific special case.
197→- The Bob-omb Battlefield proof now uses the same host-sidecar path with three data files: the extracted scene manifest, a gameplay animation document, and a display-list shader-override document. Keep live actor binding and material experiments in these sidecars instead of adding SM64-specific semantics to `kain-core` or the shared runtime.
198→
199→## Common Errors
200→
201→- The root `README.md` is useful, but live source and the built CLI are the real source of truth.
202→- The `cli` suite no longer depends on the external self-hosting fixture under `M:\Code\Other\kainselfhosting\...`; the repo-local import-c fixture under `crates/cli/tests/fixtures/import_c` is the durable regression source now.
203→- Large Windows test binaries can hit linker OOM pressure.
204→- `generated/`, `target/`, `.kain`, runtime sidecars, and compiled smoke outputs are disposable unless explicitly archived under `docs/validation/` or `docs/recent/`.
205→- The live SM64 decomp root currently sits at `M:\Code\Other\Research\sm64-master\sm64-master`, not the outer `sm64-master` folder. The older stale import reports pointed at the outer folder, which hid a real pathing mistake.
206→- The native runtime is Windows-first today. Linux and macOS surfaces exist, but much of that lane is still stubbed or partial.
207→- The compute pipeline is mid-transition from heuristic metadata to compiler-owned truth. When touching it, prefer extending bundle contracts over adding new runtime-only inference.
208→- Frontend bridge registration must be target-scoped. Host/runtime extensions that are valid for `Interpret` or `Test` must not leak into shader artifact compilation or other non-host targets, or Fabric and direct driver paths will diverge.
209→- The native shader-canvas lane is SPIR-V-canonical at the bundle level, but the current WGPU host still resolves WGSL for execution. Do not mistake that compatibility bridge for permission to move shader-canvas truth out of the emitted bundles.
210→- The native packaging loop is file-backed. If hot reload or packaged state looks stale, verify the generated `app_manifest.json`, `runtime_snapshot.json`, and launcher env vars before blaming the runtime.
211→- Fabric Python execution should stay behind `kain-python` helpers. Do not make `kain-host` reach directly into `pyo3` imports or `PythonScopeState` internals when the Python lane can expose a narrower execution API.
212→- Fabric runtime ownership is now split cleanly: `kain-omni` owns `KAIN.fabric.toml` schema/validation/report types, while `kain-host` owns local execution, dependency plumbing, and runtime adapter behavior.
213→- Fabric step inputs now flow through raw `fabric_inputs` for every runtime adapter. Kain/C/Rust glue consumes canonical host objects directly, while the Python and Node bridge crates project shared buffer/image payloads into language-native contract objects with `bytearray` and `Uint8Array` bytes views.
214→- Fabric Python and Node steps now support mixed named outputs when they return a dict/object whose fields match the manifest's declared output names. Shared outputs round-trip through the canonical host-owned interop contract family instead of falling back to string-only placeholders.
215→- Missing declared Python/Node output fields now fail with structured Fabric errors keyed as `missing_output_field`, with `output_name` recorded in failure details. Preserve that contract surface when touching adapter execution or bridge helpers.
216→- The durable end-to-end Fabric proof lives under `smoketest/fabric/polyglot_local`. It is the quickest repo-local example of Python -> Kain -> C ABI -> Rust crate -> Node execution with typed shared image/shared buffer flow.
217→- The durable GPU Fabric proof lives under `smoketest/fabric/gpu_compute_convergence`. If a Fabric GPU step succeeds through `kain gpu-artifacts` but fails through `kain fabric run`, compare `kain-driver` target registration/augmentation behavior first, then inspect Fabric residency metadata and shared-buffer shape/access inference before blaming Vulkan.
218→- `kain fabric init --template polyglot` now emits a runnable local smoke-grade scaffold, including its local Rust crate manifest and native C fixture, instead of a validation-only placeholder.
219→- Fabric host smoketests now use deterministic roots under `target/fab-init` and `target/fab-smoke`, preserving `.kain/cache` across separate `cargo test` invocations. If a rerun is still slow, the remaining wall time is usually Cargo recompilation rather than bridge cache misses inside the test body.
220→- The generated polyglot scaffold also writes `FABRIC.README.md`; treat that file as the first-stop quickstart for the smoke-grade local pipeline shape.
221→- `smoketest/allinone` is the broad regression umbrella for major CLI and bridge surfaces. Its runner is manifest-driven and clears each lane's generated outputs before rerun, so stale artifacts should not be treated as proof that a current codegen path still works.
222→- For SM64/Fast3D research, Fabric should stay an optional post-extraction simulation lane that feeds buffers or textures into the adapter. Do not make display-list extraction or the base render loop depend on Fabric before the geometry and segment path is stable.
223→
224→## Template Packs
225→
226→`templates/Web` now hosts a manifest-driven universal web starter aimed at users who should not need Rust or Cargo installed.
227→
228→Key rules for this lane:
229→
230→- Kain owns orchestration and semantic UI preview entrypoints.
231→- Node FFI owns browser packaging, local serving, and actor-server runtime glue.
232→- themes, content, scenes, and experiences are registry-driven data, not scattered starter literals.
233→- web template boilerplate should prefer reusable stdlib wrappers (`std::javascript::site_runtime`, `std::javascript::site_actor`) plus shared helper runtimes over copy-pasted starter code.
234→
235→
